note: NVIDIA's role in AI-infrastructure debt/private-credit financing, kept separate from the equity partnerships table above since the nature of involvement differs sharply by deal - explicitly labeled Direct (NVIDIA is itself a financing party) vs Indirect (NVIDIA is only the equipment supplier whose GPUs collateralize debt raised by others).

deals.name: CoreWeave capacity backstop
deals.description: NVIDIA committed to buy CoreWeave's unsold cloud capacity through April 2032 - a "buyer of last resort" guarantee, not a loan. Sits on top of NVIDIA's separate ~$2B CoreWeave equity stake; CoreWeave itself raised $7.5B of GPU-collateralized debt to buy NVIDIA chips. STILL ACTIVE as of Q3 2026 (CoreWeave's own CEO cited it again on that quarter's earnings call) - distinct and unaffected by the broader revenue-sharing program below being paused.

deals.name: "AI Compute Partnership" revenue-sharing program
deals.description: A broader, formalized version of the CoreWeave-style backstop: NVIDIA provides credit support/backstop guarantees to smaller AI clouds building out capacity, in exchange for 50% of cloud revenue above a base hourly rate threshold - on top of the normal chip sale. First named partners: Sharon AI (~40K GB300 GPUs, Australia) and Firmus Technologies (~170K GPUs, Indonesia). PAUSED after ~2 months (late Aug 2026): NVIDIA employees flagged antitrust exposure internally, and prospective partners objected to being required to route customer approval through NVIDIA. NVIDIA has left the door open to restructure or reabsorb it, and a spokesperson maintains the underlying July business model "is still in place and continues to evolve" even as new deal-signing is on hold - a genuinely unsettled, not fully-resolved, status.
deals.source: NVIDIA Blog (Jul 1 2026) / WSJ, Benzinga, The Next Web (pause reporting)

deals.name: OpenAI Ohio data center financing
deals.description: NVIDIA reported to be backing/financing an OpenAI Ohio data center. Exact structure (direct lender vs. guarantor) not confirmed in press coverage - flagged as such rather than overstated.

deals.name: Anthropic-Lambda data center lease (Hut 8)
deals.description: Anthropic signed a $35B compute deal with Lambda (an NVIDIA-backed cloud provider). NVIDIA itself holds the lease on the Nueces County, TX data center - built by Hut 8 - that houses the capacity, then supplies it to Lambda, which supplies it to Anthropic (also an NVIDIA equity holding). A single deal chains together an NVIDIA-backed customer, an NVIDIA-backed cloud, and an NVIDIA-leased building full of NVIDIA chips - the clearest single example of the circularity Barron's/WSJ have flagged.

deals.name: $500B AI infrastructure financing platform
deals.description: NVIDIA partnered with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to mobilize $500B+ of THIRD-PARTY capital. NVIDIA is not the lender/guarantor - it makes its compute an "investable asset" that these banks/asset managers underwrite and lend against. Huang has said NVIDIA retains an option to backstop up to $125B (~25%) of these deals if needed, a potential (not yet executed) direct role.
deals.status: confirmed (deals still subject to definitive agreements)

deals.name: Meta Hyperion JV (with Blue Owl)
deals.description: SPV for Meta's Louisiana Hyperion campus (2GW+): $27B A+-rated debt plus $2.5B equity, anchored by PIMCO ($18B) and BlackRock ($3B), Blue Owl owns 80%. NVIDIA is the equipment supplier only - no NVIDIA financing role disclosed.

deals.name: CoreWeave DDTL 4.0
deals.description: Delayed-draw term loan, the first investment-grade-rated GPU-collateralized debt facility (Moody's A3), priced at SOFR+225bps. NVIDIA GPUs are the collateral; NVIDIA is not a party to the loan.

circular_financing_note: CFO Colette Kress addressed "circular financing" concerns directly on the Q2 FY26 earnings call (Aug 26-27, 2026): "We recognize the scale of this support, and we know some will call this circular financing. We see it differently... our risk is limited." Huang: "the only regret... is that I didn't invest more and sooner." Skeptics remain: Mizuho said the $500B platform "doesn't quiet" concerns about underlying end-demand; Bernstein's Rasgon said the OpenAI deal "will clearly fuel 'circular' concerns." Broader context: Oracle/Meta/xAI/CoreWeave have moved ~$120B of AI infrastructure debt off-balance-sheet via SPVs; US datacenter debt issuance roughly doubled to ~$182B in 2025.
